subject.title: Feature Request: Gateway lifecycle hooks (onSubagentComplete, onToolCallThreshold, onTurnComplete)

question: Should OpenClaw expose subagent completion, turn completion, and tool-call threshold data through workspace/internal hooks, and if so what payload, authority, ordering, and threshold semantics are safe?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but this becomes a public hook/config/security boundary because it may expose session, subagent, transcript, and tool-call data and overlaps existing typed plugin lifecycle hooks.

options.title: Observation-Only Internal Events
options.body: Add narrow workspace/internal lifecycle events with minimized metadata while leaving mutation, mid-turn control, and sensitive data access in typed plugin hooks.

options.title: Keep Lifecycle Plugin-Only
options.body: Treat existing typed plugin hooks as the supported lifecycle/control surface and decline expanding HOOK.md workspace hooks for this data.

options.title: Design Unified Lifecycle Contract
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers define one lifecycle model covering internal hooks, typed plugin hooks, payloads, thresholds, permissions, and ordering.

recommendation.title: Observation-Only Internal Events
recommendation.body: Add narrow workspace/internal lifecycle events with minimized metadata while leaving mutation, mid-turn control, and sensitive data access in typed plugin hooks.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved decision sits on typed hook API boundaries and lifecycle/security semantics where recent hook contract history points to this owner.
